A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Koel-TTS study with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical manuscript content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTS experiments and human evaluations in Section 3, with additional preference-alignment, tokenization, and robustness results in Appendices B, D, and F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TTS experiments, human evaluations, and appendix results. These remain empirical outcomes produced by the work.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1-2.5 retain identical tokenization, three model architectures, training losses, DPO/RPO preference alignment, and classifier-free guidance procedures. Appendix A's ranking algorithm is also unchanged.

E1.justification: The English training mixture, six-language multilingual coverage, seen/unseen-speaker evaluations, and Appendix F's repeated-word hard-sentence scenario are identical.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains VALLE-X, YourTTS, T5-TTS, E2-TTS, F5-TTS, XTTS-v2, and StyleTTS-2. The architecture, preference-alignment, CFG, and ground-truth-as-chosen comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the 200/180-utterance seen/unseen English evaluations and 100 utterances per non-English language, with identical metrics, training settings, sampling procedures, and human-evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The architecture comparisons, ground-truth preference-pair ablation, CFG-scale analysis, DPO/RPO sensitivity comparisons, tokenizer ablations, and hard-sentence robustness tests are unchanged, including Appendices B, D, and F.

E5.justification: Both specify five repetitions per experiment and report means with 95% confidence intervals in Section 3.1. Human MOS confidence-interval reporting in Appendix C is unchanged.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1-6 and Figures 4-6 are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains multilingual Koel-TTS CER of 0.63%, WER of 1.42%, and SSIM of 0.740.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, alignment formulation, preference rewards, Pareto-ranking definition, and CFG equation are identical. No formal assumption, proof, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about preference alignment and CFG improving intelligibility, speaker similarity, naturalness, and zero-shot TTS performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of speaker generalization, preference-pair selection, automatic versus human similarity scores, CFG computational cost, and remaining hard-sentence limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A's ranking code, Appendix E's architecture and training details, hardware disclosures, evaluation documentation, and website/repository-access statements are identical.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to SpeechAlign, earlier preference-optimization methods, and prior CFG-based speech synthesis.

P1.justification: Only the arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 7 February 2025 to v2 dated 22 July 2025. The title, authors, manuscript wording, section organization, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement are identical. Rendered pages 2-15 are pixel-identical; the updated first-page margin stamp leaves the manuscript layout unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information are identical throughout the main text and appendices. Updating the arXiv stamp and PDF metadata creates no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
